In 2022, Alaska Center Resource Familys implemented Sqreen as a Web Application Firewalls (WAF) on their public website. The deployment was focused on protecting web application traffic and instrumenting application layer defenses for the organization’s site.

The implementation used Sqreen application level protection capabilities, including HTTP request inspection, rule based filtering, bot mitigation controls, and runtime application protection instrumentation. Configuration work centered on selecting and tuning rule sets, configuring event alerting, and applying automated blocking policies where applicable.

Operational scope was limited to the organization’s public web presence and associated web application components, with administrative control held by the internal IT function. Governance emphasized policy management, alert tuning, and maintaining security event logs to support incident handling and existing operational workflows.

In 2022 All American Rentime deployed Sqreen on its customer-facing website. Sqreen is installed as a Web Application Firewalls (WAF) control to provide application-layer protection for the company storefront and online forms.

That said, there are limited startups in Paris where you can work in English, and I didn't want to be involved in products I wasn't interested in, so I only applied to three companies. Two of them contacted me, and I only applied to Sqreen myself. As a result, I turned down one company, failed at another, and accepted the offer from Sqreen.

Sqreen's Selection Process
Sqreen's selection process looks like this:

Talent Sqreen (30 minute video call)Expert Sqreen (30 minute video call)Technical Sqreen (2 hour take-home assignment)Welcome to the Sqreenhouse (Half-day onsite interviews + lunch)Founder Sqreen (30 minute video call)Reference Sqreen

Next was a half-day onsite interview. I had the choice of starting with the interview and ending with lunch, or starting with lunch and ending with the interview. Since I figured I'd be too nervous to eat if I started with lunch, I asked to start with the interview, only to slightly regret it when I had to be there at 9:15 AM.
First, one of the engineers gave me a demo of the product. They gave me a rough overview of the existing features, features currently in development, and the future direction.

By the way, it seems every engineer goes through these three sessions, and it was clear that they are looking for people who not only have technical skills but also high communication skills and a product mindset.

After it was over, I had a wrapping-up session with the Head of People and the Director of the Tech team. They asked for my impressions of the day and some simple questions (Can you explain what kind of product Sqreen is? How do you learn new things? etc.), and they explained how they develop their product.

When they asked, "Is there anything you'd like to ask, about anything at all?", I asked a question I had been agonizing over since the day before: "There are only male engineers here, what do you think about that? Are you doing anything to hire female engineers?"

I was very relieved that at least they understood why the current situation was not okay and that they had concrete actions for improvement. Even so, there are still only two female engineers, and honestly, I don't want to be impressed by something like this, but the reality is that this is the level at which I feel impressed.

After that, they told me that the next steps would be a meeting in the afternoon with the people who participated in the interview, and that they might add an extra interview if there was anything they wanted to follow up on, but otherwise, the next step would be the final interview with the CEO.

The reference check proceeded simultaneously, and I submitted the contact information for my previous manager and a colleague. My colleague showed me the draft, and I almost cried because they praised me so much. Even if you aren't satisfied with where you are now, good things happen if you work hard.
